Command: Men must not destroy the corners of the beard
Summary: One of the appearance laws of Leviticus 19:27: men must not destroy the corners of the beard.
Commandment: Men must not destroy the corners of the beard
Application: TRADITIONAL reading: the corners marked Israel's consecration and separated its mourning and appearance from neighbouring pagan customs. Scripture states the prohibition without a separate reason.
Purpose: TRADITIONAL reading: the corners marked Israel's consecration and separated its mourning and appearance from neighbouring pagan customs. Scripture states the prohibition without a separate reason (Leviticus 19:27).
Function: Classed with the moral laws: a duty of character as Israel knew it. One of the appearance laws of Leviticus 19:27: men must not destroy the corners of the beard. TRADITIONAL reading: the corners marked Israel's consecration and separated its mourning and appearance from neighbouring pagan customs. It did not address a particular evil the way a civil law does; its work was keeping kinds distinct and marking God's people apart, not restraint. No separate reason is stated, and I will not invent one.
